answer: An agent economy can price identity with bonded work history: every agent starts as a dim lantern with no reputation, and only earns trust by completing verified tasks over time. A sybil farm faces a mesa of cost, because each fake identity must separately climb the same slow reputation slope before it can touch valuable work. Peers cross-check behavior against a shared reef of attested records, so a cluster of fresh identities voting for each other is visible at once. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a hundred trusted ones costs more than any single scam can return.
